title: Surge Capacity Sensitivity Planner
description: Working spreadsheet to test sensitivity of our cost model to short-duration traffic surges and microbursts. Focus is on mapping peak QPS and sequence-length distributions to GPU allocations (reserve vs burst) and monthly spend estimates. Intended to feed Optimize recommendations and Dedicated capacity sizing proposals.
objective: Provide a compact, scenario-driven view for product and finance to understand cost delta between reserved GPUs, burst-on-demand, and hybrid burst pools for short (minutes-hours) surges. Surface tipping points where reserved capacity + automatic fallback is cheaper than aggressive burst usage.
assumptions: Baseline token pricing: $0.0006 per 1k tokens served (model compute unit estimate)
On-demand GPU rate: $3.25 / GPU-hour equivalent in our cost model (includes infra + amortized infra ops)
Reserved GPU effective rate: $1.95 / GPU-hour when committed monthly
Average user request tokens: variable by scenario (see table)
KV/prefix cache hit reduces per-request latency but counted as reducing token compute by hit_fraction
Autoscaling warmup: 90s cold-start window adds 20% overhead for first minute of surge for new GPU allocations
methodology: Take peak QPS and sequence length distribution, compute tokens_per_second, map to sustained GPU throughput using per-GPU tokens/sec envelope for our model family (emu: 120k tokens/sec for 2k context avg). Add 10-25% headroom depending on SLO. Convert required GPUs to cost under reserved and on-demand pricing. For microbursts (<15 minutes) model cost amortizes differently: include startup overhead and minimum billing increments.
scenarios: baseline: steady growth, small headroom target (SLO 95/500ms), assumed normal cache behavior
holiday_spike: multi-hour elevated QPS driven by seasonal traffic, high avg seq length due to long-form generation
promo_campaign: sustained high QPS for 8-24 hours, high variance in sequence length and lower cache effectiveness
cache_failure: cache degraded, leads to higher compute per request and exposes reserve sizing fragility
microburst_short: intense 5-15 minute microbursts (ads/flash-sale), cost dominated by minimum billing increments and cold-start overhead
interpretation_summary: Preliminary results show reserved capacity becomes cost-effective when expected sustained hours exceed ~2,000 GPU-hours per month per pool; for short microbursts (<1 hour) on-demand often cheaper unless we maintain a small hot pool. Cache failures materially increase cost—consider automated degraded-mode routing to cheaper smaller models when cache hit drops below 20%.
recommendations: Maintain a small hot reserve pool sized for 5-10% of expected peak QPS to absorb microbursts and lower cold-start overhead
Use hybrid billing: reserve core pool, enable burst on-demand above 70% utilization with automatic scale-down after 10 min
Implement degraded-model fallback during cache outages to cap per-request compute and avoid quadratic cost increases
Add tagging to traffic sources so cost attribution by campaign/marketing ID is immediate (enable chargeback)
action_items: (Owner: Marco) Build a CI job to regenerate this sheet weekly with last 30d QPS and token distributions
(Owner: Jia) Add explicit minimum-billing-minute model for each cloud provider and run sensitivity across 1/5/15/60 minute increments
(Owner: Tess) Validate per-GPU tokens/sec envelope for the new quantized model family (Q4-2024 onboarded models)
(Owner: Laura) Draft short one-pager for Finance showing tipping points for reserve vs burst to use in pricing discussion
risks_and_open_questions: How accurate are our per-GPU throughput envelopes for newly quantized weights? Need bench runs. Also need to confirm legal/commit terms for reserved pools when we suggest monthly commit changes. What SLA delta do product teams accept when using degraded fallback?
notes: This sheet is intentionally compact — prefer quick scenario toggles over exhaustive parameterization. Next step: plug into Optimize's recommendation engine and run Monte Carlo of demand tail risks. Keep draft public to eng-optimize and finance for comment.
